cues: Valve combinations provide alternate fingerings, making awkward passages easier to play in tune.
The instrument is commonly built in B-flat, with longer tubing than higher-pitched piccolo models.
A small water key releases condensation gathered inside the brass tubing during performances.
Some versions add a fourth valve, giving performers extra low notes and alternate fingerings.
Lacquered or silver-plated finishes protect the brass surface and give the exterior distinct appearances.
A lightweight body can be held horizontally, supported by one hand while the other operates its controls.
